title: PolarDepth: Monocular Transparent Object Depth from Polar-Physics Priors
claim: Standard depth estimators and active sensors fail on transparent objects; adding polarization-derived geometric priors recovers complete, accurate depth for downstream use.
layout: Single wide row, left-to-right, two flows with red zoom-in boxes
description: A wide single-row figure. On the far left, two stacked depth maps, from Depth Anything V2 and an Intel RealSense D435i, are marked with red boxes over the transparent region. Next to them are two parallel input-to-output flows. The top flow takes an RGB photo of toys and blocks, passes it through 'Foundational Inference', and produces an Initial Depth map. The bottom flow takes a noisy polarization image and passes it through a dark red 'Geometric Decoding' step to give a black surface-normal-style 'Geometry Constraints' render of a transparent object. Both flows merge in 'Depth Recovery & Refinement', which outputs a Depth Output map. Red dotted zoom lines link the boxed regions to an 'Incomplete Depth' inset and a sharper 'Complete Depth' inset. A real robot-grasping photo sits at the far right. Rainbow depth colormaps dominate the visual weight.
caption: Transparent objects challenge conventional depth estimation, leading to failure in both learning-based methods like Depth Anything V2 (Yang et al., 2024) and active sensors such as Intel RealSense D435i. In contrast, polarization cues provide reliable geometric patterns even in transparent regions. The proposed PolarDepth extracts physically grounded geometric priors from these cues to recover accurate and complete depth, enabling precise robotic grasping and robust transparent object understanding.
abstract: Depth estimation for transparent objects remains a fundamental challenge, as RGB-based cues often fail in regions affected by refraction and light transmission. Polarization provides physically grounded information related to surface orientation and material properties, offering reliable geometric cues even in the absence of texture. In this work, we introduce PolarDepth, a monocular framework that incorporates both RGB and polarization inputs, including the degree and angle of linear polarization (DoLP and AoLP), to estimate dense depth and localize transparent regions. PolarDepth injects polarization-derived physical priors by estimating the refractive index, zenith angle, and azimuth angle from polarization measurements and embedding them into an implicit geometric representation that constrains depth inference in ambiguous transparent regions. To support model development and evaluation, we introduce PTOD, a dataset with synchronized RGB, polarization, and depth data and manually annotated transparent region masks. Experimental results demonstrate that PolarDepth achieves state-of-the-art performance in transparent object depth estimation. The findings highlight the effectiveness of embedding polarization-derived physical priors into learned representations for robust perception in complex visual environments.
